_meta.indication: Treatment of severe hypoglycemia in pediatric and adult patients with diabetes aged 6 years and above.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, parallel-arm, placebo- and active-controlled (GlucaGen) trial with 2:1:1 randomization, using a hypoglycemic clamp to induce hypoglycemia.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM) undergoing insulin-induced hypoglycemia.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Time to plasma glucose recovery, defined as first increase in plasma glucose of ≥ 20 mg/dL from baseline without administration of rescue IV glucose.
pivotal_trials.result: Median time to plasma glucose recovery 10 minutes [10, 10] with dasiglucagon vs 40 minutes [30, 40] with placebo; p<0.001 (log-rank).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled parallel-arm trial using an auto-injector formulation and a hypoglycemic clamp.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM) undergoing insulin-induced hypoglycemia.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Time to plasma glucose recovery (first increase ≥ 20 mg/dL from baseline without rescue IV glucose).
pivotal_trials.result: Median time to plasma glucose recovery 10 minutes [8, 12] with dasiglucagon vs 35 minutes [20, ∞) with placebo; p<0.001 (log-rank).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-controlled (GlucaGen) parallel-arm trial with a hypoglycemic clamp, using a pre-filled syringe.
pivotal_trials.population: Pediatric patients ≥ 6 years and < 18 years with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Time to plasma glucose recovery (first increase ≥ 20 mg/dL from baseline without rescue IV glucose).
pivotal_trials.result: Median time to plasma glucose recovery 10 minutes [8, 12] with dasiglucagon vs 30 minutes [20, ∞) with placebo; p<0.001 (log-rank).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥2%) in adults: nausea (57% vs 4% placebo), vomiting (25% vs 2%), headache (11% vs 4%), diarrhea (5% vs 0%), and injection site pain (2% vs 0%). In pediatrics: nausea, vomiting, headache, and injection site pain.
target_moa: Dasiglucagon is a glucagon receptor agonist that increases blood glucose by activating hepatic glucagon receptors, stimulating glycogen breakdown and release of glucose from the liver.
modality: Peptide (glucagon analog); dasiglucagon is comprised of 29 amino acids.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; outside expertise was not necessary and there were no controversial issues.

basis.text: The application was designated Standard (not Priority) review.

summary.text: Zegalogue was submitted as a 505(b)(1) NDA with standard review, received March 27, 2020, and approved March 22, 2021 for treatment of severe hypoglycemia in patients aged 6 years and above, based on three pivotal placebo-controlled Phase III trials; no advisory committee was convened and a deferred pediatric PMR was required for ages 1 to <6 years.

citations.quote: Please refer to your new drug application (NDA) dated and received March 27, 2020, and your amendments, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for Zegalogue (dasiglucagon) injection.
ZEGALOGUE® is indicated for the treatment of severe hypoglycemia in pediatric and adult patients with diabetes aged 6 years and above.

Your application for Zegalogue was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because outside expertise was not necessary; there were no controversial issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion.

requirement.text: PMR 4034-1: Conduct an open-label pediatric study to evaluate the safety, efficacy, and PK/PD of dasiglucagon in pediatric patients ages 1 year to <6 years with type 1 diabetes mellitus (deferred pediatric study required under section 505B(a) / PREA).

citations.quote: 4034-1 Conduct an open-label pediatric study to evaluate the safety, efficacy, and pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics of dasiglucagon in pediatric patients ages 1 year to <6 years with type 1 diabetes mellitus.

Your deferred pediatric study required by section 505B(a) of the FDCA is a required postmarketing study. The status of this postmarketing study must be reported annually according to 21 CFR 314.81 and section 505B(a)(4)(C) of the FDCA. This required study is listed below.
